title: Tolerate fake compression pointers in DNS record data
answers: Why does decompressing a DNS SOA record fail?
How should DNS record decompression handle bytes that resemble compression pointers?
Preserve numeric record data while expanding compressed domain names
body:
Symptom: Decompressing a DNS SOA record fails when numeric data resembles a domain-name compression pointer.
Root cause: mitmproxy/net/dns/domain_names.py:decompress_from_record_data treats bytes with the pointer-indicator bits as candidates and previously let struct.error from attempted decompression escape.
Fix pattern: Catch struct.error around candidate decoding and replacement; leave failed candidates unchanged and advance one byte so scanning continues. Successfully decoded pointers still expand normally.
Constraints: This fallback applies to scanning mixed record data, where pointer-like bytes can belong to other data types. It catches struct.error only and does not detect false pointers that decode successfully; regression coverage is in test/mitmproxy/net/dns/test_domain_names.py:test_record_data_contains_fake_pointer.
applies: DNS resource-record data decompression that scans for compression pointers among other data types.
